row.title: Snaky
row.statement: The quantity is the upper bound on Maker moves needed to win Snaky on the infinite square board. Fewer moves are better. Nándor Sieben’s finite \(17\times17\) strategy, supplied by gotrevor, also works on the infinite board. The separate \(15\times15\) result concerns board size.

current.conditions: Extends Sieben's 20-move strategy with tactics from Trevor Morris's 15×15 work; also wins on \(17\times 17\).
current.proofScope: Author-run Lean 4.34.1 audit: Snaky.snaky_wins_plane_in_19 (every legal Breaker reply on the infinite board) and the 17×17 theorem use only the standard axioms; no independent rerun.

relevantRepos.name: gotrevor/snaky-15x15
relevantRepos.note: The separate finite-board results place the smallest Maker-winning board side between 10 and 15. The \(9\times 9\) Breaker claim has a certificate and Python checker, but no Lean proof.

candidates.decision: Selected: no trusted statement; prior audit establishes a distinct theorem, not this target
